statement: A box plot of the scores on a science test has these five values: minimum $52$, first quartile $64$, median $71$, third quartile $80$ and maximum $97$. About what percent of the students scored between $64$ and $97$?

choices.misconception: I thought the stretch from 64 to 97 was only one section of the box plot, so I said 25%, but it covers three sections.
I subtracted 64 from 97 to get 33 and called that the percent, but the difference between scores is not a share of the students.
I remembered that the box holds 50% of the data and stopped there, forgetting the upper whisker from 80 to 97 adds another 25%.

hints: The five values of a box plot split the data into four groups. About what share of the data is in each group?
Each of the four sections (min to $Q_1$, $Q_1$ to median, median to $Q_3$, $Q_3$ to max) holds about $25\%$ of the scores. How many sections lie between $64$ and $97$?
From $64$ (the first quartile) to $97$ (the maximum) covers the box and the upper whisker: three sections of $25\%$.

solutions.reliable: The value $64$ is the first quartile, so about $25\%$ of the scores are below it. The maximum $97$ is the top of the data. So about $100\% - 25\% = 75\%$ of the students scored between $64$ and $97$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
